l-m-m3-b01-01.title: Sum of irrational numbers always be irrational?
l-m-m3-b01-01.goal: Check if claim say sum of two irrational numbers always be irrational true, and find and explain one case wey no true (counterexample).
l-m-m3-b01-01.material: Claim: When you add two irrational numbers, the sum always be irrational too. Find addition wey show say claim wrong.
l-m-m3-b01-01.s.s1.r.a: The sum √2+√3 also irrational. E fit the claim.
l-m-m3-b01-01.s.s1.r.c: √8=2√2, so sum 3√2 also irrational. E fit the claim.
l-m-m3-b01-01.s.s1.r.d: Sum 3√5 also irrational. E fit the claim.
l-m-m3-b01-01.s.s1.explain: √2+(−√2)=0 na rational number. The sum fit be rational, so the claim fail.
l-m-m3-b01-01.s.s2.model.0: √2 and −√2 both irrational, but their sum na 0, and 0 rational, so e go against the claim.
l-m-m3-b01-01.s.s2.model.1: Adding two irrational numbers wey only differ by sign give 0, so the sum no always irrational.

l-m-m3-b01-02.title: Quadratic equation always get real solution?
l-m-m3-b01-02.goal: Check if claim say quadratic equation always get real solution true, and find and explain one case wey no true (counterexample).
l-m-m3-b01-02.material: Claim: Quadratic equation always get at least one real solution. Find equation wey show say claim wrong.
l-m-m3-b01-02.s.s1.r.a: x=3 or x=−3 na solution. E fit the claim.
l-m-m3-b01-02.s.s1.r.b: x=2 na solution. E fit the claim.
l-m-m3-b01-02.s.s1.r.d: x=3 or x=−1 na solution. E fit the claim.
l-m-m3-b01-02.s.s1.explain: x²+4=0 mean x²=−4, but square of real number no fit be negative, so no real solution dey.
l-m-m3-b01-02.s.s2.model.0: It need x²=−4, but square of real number na 0 or more, so no real solution. E be counterexample.
l-m-m3-b01-02.s.s2.model.1: Other choices all get solutions, but x²+4 always at least 4 and no fit become 0, so e be counterexample.

l-m-m3-b01-03.title: Quadratic expression always fit factor over integers?
l-m-m3-b01-03.goal: Check if claim say x²+bx+c always fit factor with integers p and q true, and find and explain one case wey no true (counterexample).
l-m-m3-b01-03.material: Claim: Quadratic expression of form x²+bx+c always fit factor as (x+p)(x+q) by finding integers p and q. Find expression wey show say claim wrong.
l-m-m3-b01-03.s.s1.r.a: E factor as (x+2)(x+3). E fit the claim.
l-m-m3-b01-03.s.s1.r.b: E factor as (x−3)(x+2). E fit the claim.
l-m-m3-b01-03.s.s1.r.c: E factor as (x+3)(x−3). E fit the claim.
l-m-m3-b01-03.s.s1.explain: For x²+x+1, no two integers get total 1 and product 1, so e no fit factor with integers p and q.
l-m-m3-b01-03.s.s2.model.0: No two integers get total 1 and product 1, so x²+x+1 no fit write as (x+p)(x+q).
l-m-m3-b01-03.s.s2.model.1: For the other expressions, you fit find two integers p and q; only x²+x+1 no get them, so e be counterexample.

l-m-m3-b01-04.title: Value of trigonometric ratio always be 1 or less?
l-m-m3-b01-04.goal: Check if claim say value of trigonometric ratio always 1 or less true, and find and explain one case wey no true (counterexample).
l-m-m3-b01-04.material: Claim: When 0°<A<90°, values of sin A, cos A and tan A all always 1 or less. Find trigonometric ratio wey show say claim wrong.
l-m-m3-b01-04.s.s1.prompt: Choose trigonometric ratio wey go against claim (counterexample).
l-m-m3-b01-04.s.s1.r.a: Opposite side shorter than hypotenuse, so sin 70°<1. E fit claim.
l-m-m3-b01-04.s.s1.r.c: Adjacent side shorter than hypotenuse, so cos 20°<1. E fit claim.
l-m-m3-b01-04.s.s1.r.d: tan 30°≈0.58 na 1 or less. E fit claim.
l-m-m3-b01-04.s.s1.explain: tan 60°=√3≈1.73, wey bigger than 1. If opposite side longer than adjacent side, tan bigger than 1.
l-m-m3-b01-04.s.s2.model.0: tan 60°=√3≈1.73, bigger than 1, so e go against the claim say all trigonometric ratios 1 or less.
l-m-m3-b01-04.s.s2.model.1: tan na height÷base, so when height longer than base, e pass 1. That make tan 60° a counterexample.

l-m-m3-b02-01.title: Di graph of a quadratic function always meet di x-axis?
l-m-m3-b02-01.goal: Check whether claim "Graph of quadratic function always meet x-axis" dey true, and find and explain case wey no (counterexample).
l-m-m3-b02-01.material: Claim: graph of quadratic function always meet x-axis at one or more points. Find quadratic function wey show this wrong.
l-m-m3-b02-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose quadratic function wey go against claim (counterexample).
l-m-m3-b02-01.s.s1.r.a: E meet x-axis at x=2 and x=−2. This example follow claim.
l-m-m3-b02-01.s.s1.r.b: Vertex (1, 0) dey on x-axis, so graph meet. Example follow claim.
l-m-m3-b02-01.s.s1.r.d: E meet x-axis at x=3 and x=−3. This example follow claim.
l-m-m3-b02-01.s.s1.explain: y=(x−2)²+1 get vertex at (2, 1) and open up, so y≥1 and never touch x-axis.
l-m-m3-b02-01.s.s2.model.0: (x−2)²≥0, so y always at least 1 and never meet x-axis (y=0).
l-m-m3-b02-01.s.s2.model.1: Vertex (2, 1) above x-axis and graph open up, so whole graph above x-axis; this be counterexample.

l-m-m3-b02-04.material: Claim: When comparing two right triangles, the one with longer hypotenuse also get longer height. Find two triangles wey show claim wrong.

l-m-m3-b02-05.goal: Check whether claim "If √a×√b natural number, then a and b both square numbers" always true, and find and explain a counterexample.

l-m-m3-b04-06.s.s1.r.b: 25 and 25, same. This example follow claim.
l-m-m3-b04-06.s.s1.r.c: 0 and 0, same. This example follow claim.

l-m-m3-b04-06.s.s2.model.1: (a−b)²=a²−2ab+b², so dem differ when b no be 0 and a≠b. 3 and 1 be example, so counterexample.

l-m-m3-b03-28.title: Putting variance formula into words
l-m-m3-b03-28.goal: Change the variance formula into another form (expression, table, picture, or words), and explain why e mean same thing.
l-m-m3-b03-28.material: Variance na (sum of squared differences from mean)÷(number of values). You wan explain this formula in words.
l-m-m3-b03-28.s.s1.prompt: Which statement mean the same as the formula?
l-m-m3-b03-28.s.s1.o.a: The average of how far each value dey from the mean, squared
l-m-m3-b03-28.s.s1.o.b: The average of squares of each value
l-m-m3-b03-28.s.s1.r.b: You square the values themselves, no be their differences from mean.
l-m-m3-b03-28.s.s1.o.c: The sum of all differences from mean divided by number of values
l-m-m3-b03-28.s.s1.r.c: The sum of differences from mean always na 0, so you no fit leave out the squaring.
l-m-m3-b03-28.s.s1.o.d: The biggest value minus the smallest value
l-m-m3-b03-28.s.s1.r.d: That one na range. E no be variance.
l-m-m3-b03-28.s.s1.explain: Square the differences from mean, add all the squares, and divide by number of values to get variance.
l-m-m3-b03-28.s.s2.model.0: Variance na the sum of squared differences divided by number of values, so you fit call am average of squared differences.
l-m-m3-b03-28.s.s2.model.1: Variance square how far every value dey from mean, then average am. So e show how spread out the values be.

l-m-m3-b03-29.title: Describing equal-length chords using distance
l-m-m3-b03-29.goal: Change two equal-length chords in one circle into another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why e mean the same thing.
l-m-m3-b03-29.material: For one circle, chord AB and CD get same length. Describe this fact using the distances from circle centre O to the two chords.
l-m-m3-b03-29.s.s1.o.a: The chord farther from centre O longer
l-m-m3-b03-29.s.s1.r.a: The farther the chord from centre, the shorter e be.
l-m-m3-b03-29.s.s1.o.b: The two chords parallel to each other
l-m-m3-b03-29.s.s1.r.b: The chords no need be parallel even if their lengths equal.
l-m-m3-b03-29.s.s1.o.c: The two chords meet at one point
l-m-m3-b03-29.s.s1.r.c: The chords no need meet even if their lengths equal.
l-m-m3-b03-29.s.s1.o.d: The two chords dey the same distance from centre O
l-m-m3-b03-29.s.s1.explain: For one circle, chords at same distance from centre get same length. If their lengths equal, their distances equal too.
l-m-m3-b03-29.s.s2.model.0: If the chords get equal distance from centre, sides of the right triangles equal, so half of each chord equal and the chords get same length.
l-m-m3-b03-29.s.s2.model.1: The farther from centre, the shorter the chord. So if their lengths equal, their distances from centre must equal too.

l-m-m3-b03-30.title: Writing kite height using string length and angle
l-m-m3-b03-30.goal: Change kite height into another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why e mean same thing.
l-m-m3-b03-30.material: Kite string length L dey stretched straight and make angle θ with ground. If kite height na h, express h using L and trigonometric ratio.
l-m-m3-b03-30.s.s1.r.b: tan θ na height÷horizontal distance, so e no fit use string length.
l-m-m3-b03-30.s.s1.r.c: cos θ na ground distance divided by string length.
l-m-m3-b03-30.s.s1.r.d: Division go make the height bigger than string length, wey no make sense.
l-m-m3-b03-30.s.s1.explain: sin θ=height÷string length, so h=L×sin θ.
l-m-m3-b03-30.s.s2.model.0: sin θ na height divided by string length, wey be hypotenuse. Multiply both sides by L to get h=L×sin θ.
l-m-m3-b03-30.s.s2.model.1: String na hypotenuse and height na opposite side, so use sin θ=opposite÷hypotenuse, giving h=L×sin θ.

l-m-m3-b04-14.goal: Change statement that product of two consecutive natural numbers na 56 into other form (expression, table, picture, words) and explain why same meaning.

l-m-m3-b04-25.title: Changing ramp slope into trigonometric ratios
l-m-m3-b04-25.goal: Change ramp with height 3 and horizontal distance 4 into another form (expression, table, picture, words), and explain why e mean the same thing.

l-m-m3-b05-24.s.s1.prompt: Wetin be di value of tan A?
l-m-m3-b05-24.s.s1.r.b: Na hypotenuse÷base be that. tan na height÷base.
l-m-m3-b05-24.s.s1.r.d: Dis na di value of cos A.
l-m-m3-b05-24.s.s1.explain: If di base na 5 and di hypotenuse na 13, di height na √(169−25)=12, and tan A=12/5.
l-m-m3-b05-24.s.s2.model.0: If cos A=5/13, we fit take di base as 5 and di hypotenuse as 13, so di height na 12 and tan A=12/5.
l-m-m3-b05-24.s.s2.model.1: By Pythagorean theorem, di height na √(13²−5²)=12, so tan A=height/base=12/5.

l-m-m3-b01-31.s.s1.r.a: No pair of integers get product −1 and sum −1, so this method no work.

l-m-m3-b01-31.s.s2.model.1: You fit use quadratic formula for any quadratic equation, so for this equation wey no factor, Eul method fit.

l-m-m3-b01-32.s.s2.model.1: Eul 4.26 come from estimate √2≈1.41, so if exact value needed, use Gap 3√2.

l-m-m3-b01-34.title: If angles equal, all four points dey on one circle?
l-m-m3-b01-34.topic: Condition for four points to lie on one circle
l-m-m3-b01-34.goal: Compare two methods or claims about whether four points dey on one circle when two angles equal. Choose the better one and explain your thinking.
l-m-m3-b01-34.material: Two points P and Q dey on same side of line AB, and ∠APB=∠AQB. Gap say A, B, P, Q dey on one circle; Eul say equal angles alone no prove dem on one circle.
l-m-m3-b01-34.s.s1.o.a: Eul: Even if angles equal, you no fit say the points on one circle
l-m-m3-b01-34.s.s1.r.a: If inscribed angles on same side equal, the points dey on one circle.
l-m-m3-b01-34.s.s1.o.b: The points must dey on opposite sides of line AB
l-m-m3-b01-34.s.s1.r.b: If dem dey on opposite sides, the points dey on one circle when both angles total 180°.
l-m-m3-b01-34.s.s1.o.c: You need know length of AB to decide
l-m-m3-b01-34.s.s1.r.c: Whatever AB length be, if angles equal, the points dey on one circle.
l-m-m3-b01-34.s.s1.o.d: Gap: Equal angles on same side mean one circle
l-m-m3-b01-34.s.s1.explain: If segment AB dey seen from same side at equal angles, the four points dey on one circle (the reverse of inscribed angle property).
l-m-m3-b01-34.s.s2.model.0: P and Q see AB at same angle from same side of AB, so all four points dey on one circle.
l-m-m3-b01-34.s.s2.model.1: Points on circle see the same arc at same angle, so by the reverse rule, Gap correct.

l-m-m3-b04-24.title: The side opposite 30° na sin or cos?

l-m-m3-b04-24.s.s1.r.c: The two expressions get different values, so dem both no fit be right.

l-m-m3-b04-24.s.s2.model.0: Find opposite side by multiplying hypotenuse by sin, so 8×sin 30°=4.

l-m-m3-b05-08.title: Wetin Don Factor Reach di End: 2x²−8?
l-m-m3-b05-08.goal: Compare two ways, or two claims, to factor 2x²−8, choose di better one, and explain di reason.
l-m-m3-b05-08.material: Dem factor 2x²−8. A: 2(x−2)(x+2). B: (x−2)(2x+4). When you expand both, dem give 2x²−8. Find di one wey dem factor reach where dem no fit group anything again.
l-m-m3-b05-08.s.s1.prompt: Which one don factor reach di end?
l-m-m3-b05-08.s.s1.o.a: Na only A dem factor reach di end
l-m-m3-b05-08.s.s1.o.b: Na only B dem factor reach di end
l-m-m3-b05-08.s.s1.r.b: Dem fit group B's 2x+4 one more time as 2(x+2).
l-m-m3-b05-08.s.s1.o.c: Dem factor both reach di end
l-m-m3-b05-08.s.s1.r.c: Dem fit group B's 2x+4 one more time using common factor 2.
l-m-m3-b05-08.s.s1.r.d: When you expand both, dem give 2x²−8, so no one wrong.
l-m-m3-b05-08.s.s1.explain: Dem fit factor B's 2x+4 more as 2(x+2), so di final answer go be A. Dem no fit group A again.
l-m-m3-b05-08.s.s2.model.0: B's 2x+4 get common factor 2, and dem fit group am one more time, so dem never factor B reach di end, but dem factor A reach di end.
l-m-m3-b05-08.s.s2.model.1: Di 2, (x−2), and (x+2) for A no fit group again, so A na di expression wey dem factor reach di end.

l-m-m3-b05-16.material: Dem find di minimum value of y=x²−6x+5 two ways. A: put symmetry axis x=3 inside to get 9−18+5=−4. B: y=0 for x-intercepts x=1, 5, so di minimum na 0.

l-m-m3-b05-16.s.s2.model.1: Di graph curve down and di vertex dey on di symmetry axis, so −4 for x=3 na di minimum.

l-m-m3-b05-21.title: How sin and cos Dey Change as Angle Dey Bigger?
l-m-m3-b05-21.goal: Compare two ways, or two claims, about how sin A and cos A change from 0° to 90°, choose di better one, and explain di reason.
l-m-m3-b05-21.material: Compare di changes as angle A dey bigger from 0° to 90°. A: sin A dey bigger and cos A dey smaller. B: both sin A and cos A dey bigger.

l-m-m3-b05-21.s.s1.r.c: B claim say “cos A too dey bigger” wrong.

l-m-m3-b05-21.s.s2.model.1: As di angle dey bigger, di height dey grow and di base dey reduce, so sin dey bigger and cos dey smaller.

l-m-m3-b0s6-13.title: (a−b)² and (b−a)² na di same?
l-m-m3-b0s6-13.goal: Compare two methods or claims about relationship between (a−b)² and (b−a)², choose di more suitable one, and explain your reason.
l-m-m3-b0s6-13.material: Jian: (a−b)² and (b−a)² na numbers wey only differ for sign. Doha: No, di two always dey di same. Calculate both expressions when a=5, b=2 and decide who correct.
l-m-m3-b0s6-13.s.s1.o.a: Doha: di two expressions always dey di same
l-m-m3-b0s6-13.s.s1.o.b: Jian: di two expressions only differ for sign
l-m-m3-b0s6-13.s.s1.r.b: (a−b)²=9 and (b−a)²=9, so di signs dey di same. Square no dey negative.
l-m-m3-b0s6-13.s.s1.r.c: Dem dey opposite claims, so both no fit correct.
l-m-m3-b0s6-13.s.s1.o.d: E depend on values of a and b
l-m-m3-b0s6-13.s.s1.r.d: When dem expand am, both become a²−2ab+b², so dem dey di same no matter di values.
l-m-m3-b0s6-13.s.s1.explain: b−a=−(a−b), and (−m)²=m². So (a−b)²=(b−a)² always dey true.
l-m-m3-b0s6-13.s.s2.model.0: b−a na a−b times −1, and squaring remove di sign, so (a−b)²=(b−a)². For 5 and 2, both na 9 too.
l-m-m3-b0s6-13.s.s2.model.1: For a=5, b=2, 3²=9 and (−3)²=9 dey di same, and when dem expand, both na a²−2ab+b², so Doha correct.

l-m-m3-b0s6-14.title: Two ways to show √6×√24=12
l-m-m3-b0s6-14.goal: Compare two methods to find value of √6×√24, choose di more suitable one, and explain why.
l-m-m3-b0s6-14.material: Seoa write √6×√24=√144=12. Raon multiply √6≈2.449 and √24≈4.899 and get about 11.998, then talk say na 12. Decide which method better to show say na exactly 12.
l-m-m3-b0s6-14.s.s1.o.b: Raon: multiply dem as decimal numbers to get about 12
l-m-m3-b0s6-14.s.s1.r.b: Product of approximate values only dey near 12. E no fit show say na exactly 12.
l-m-m3-b0s6-14.s.s1.r.c: Approximate values get error, so dem no fit show "exactly".
l-m-m3-b0s6-14.s.s1.r.d: If you use √a×√b=√(ab), you fit find exact value.
l-m-m3-b0s6-14.s.s1.explain: √a×√b=√(ab) and 144=12², so na exactly 12. Decimal product only dey near 12, like 11.998.
l-m-m3-b0s6-14.s.s2.model.0: √6×√24=√144 and 12²=144, so na exactly 12. Decimal product na 11.998, small different from 12.
l-m-m3-b0s6-14.s.s2.model.1: Using approximate values create error, so you only know say e dey around 12, but joining roots give √144=12, wey exact.

l-m-m3-b02-39.s.s2.model.1: 10 m and 12 m too steep and pass 5°, while 18 m too long and pass 15 m. So 14 m correct.
